one_month_reasoning: The one big event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings. Intel has still not announced the date: its IR feed's latest release is from Sept 8 and EDGAR shows no 8-K [25][26]. Aggregators estimate Oct 22 [21]. Intel announced the Q2 date 23 days ahead (June 30 for July 23) [26], so having no notice by Oct 2 makes a slightly later print (Oct 27-30) a little more likely. I put about 85% on the print landing inside the window, the same as round 1. Guidance is $15.8-16.8B revenue and $0.38 non-GAAP EPS [3]. Consensus is $0.39 or higher after many upward revisions [2], so the bar has gone up. The supervisor re-checked my reaction base rate against daily prices: 8 of the last 11 next-day moves were negative, with a mean absolute move of about 11% [18]. Correction from round 1: no ~$15B follow-on is planned. That figure was the original proposed size of the August deal [23][24], and EDGAR shows no new offering filing [25]. The real dilution risk is narrower: Intel's company lock-up ends at the Q3 release [22], so a new raise becomes possible in the last week of October, but nothing is filed and I give it about 10%. The stock is up +34% in September at about 58x FY27 EPS. Momentum base rates for semis after a 35%+ month on top of a 100%+ year (median about +5%, inflated by survivorship [17]) roughly offset the sell-the-news habit. Net: median about $119 (flat to slightly down), lognormal with a monthly sigma of 0.21 (about 76%/3.5, since earnings vol is already part of realized vol). No index events or regulatory decisions are scheduled in the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of a forward P/E (FY2028E EPS $2.70 x 35x, cut ~1% for escrow-share dilution = $93.6, weight 0.6) and EV/sales (FY2028E revenue $82B x 7x = $574B EV, less ~$25B of net debt plus NCI, over 5.45B shares = $100.7, weight 0.4), for about $96 as the value 12 months out. That is about 20% below the $120 price.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2028E EPS $2.70 x 35x NTM P/E x (5.40/5.45 escrow dilution) = $93.6; NCI is already excluded from EPS attributable to Intel

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus of $2.06 grown about 31%, close to the consensus FY26-to-FY27 growth (+36%, $1.52 to $2.06) with a little fade. Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.42 and the $0.38 Q3 guide [3] already annualize to about $1.60, which supports the trajectory.

Set above NVDA (28x) and TSMC's 10-year average (about 23x) [4] because Intel's EPS is growing off a depressed base and supply is constrained. It is well below today's 58-62x FY27 [4][1]. Intel's own history (P/S 1.5-12.5x over a decade [5]) shows peak multiples do not last, and the 2000 peak at about 50x EPS was followed by an 82% drawdown [19].

Consensus EPS is on roughly 5.40B diluted shares (5,285M basic after the full greenshoe [6][22] plus 119M RSUs/PSUs). I add about 50M of the 143M DoC escrow shares, which are released as Secure Enclave disbursements arrive [22]. That is a ~1% haircut. The phantom ~$15B follow-on I counted in round 1 is removed.

methods.name: EV/sales

inputs_detail.derivation: $72B FY27 consensus grown about 14%, slowing from consensus FY26-to-FY27 growth of about 14% ($63.1B to $72.0B) and Q2's +25% YoY [3].

Near the middle of Intel's decade P/S range of 1.5-12.5x [5] and below today's 11.7x EV/revenue [1]. Non-GAAP gross margin of about 42% [3] is far below NVDA/TSM levels, so a top-of-range multiple is hard to justify a year out.

inputs_detail.input: Net claims ahead of common (net debt + NCI)
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 cash plus ST investments of $29.7B plus $22.62B net offering proceeds (with the greenshoe) gives $52.3B, against $50.5B of debt, so about $1.8B net cash pro forma [3][22]. Less about $10B of H2-2026 cash burn (Q2 adj. FCF was -$8.4B [3]) gives about $8-9B net debt. Add the $15.6B non-controlling interest from the 424B5 capitalization table [22] for about $25B. Round 1 used ~$5B, which wrongly used $19.7B of proceeds and left out the NCI.

5,285M basic after the full 31.6M-share greenshoe [6][22], plus 119M unvested RSUs/PSUs (5.40B), plus about 50M of the 143M escrow shares likely released within 12 months. The 241M warrants are excluded because they only become exercisable if Intel's foundry ownership falls below 51% [22]. No follow-on is included: none is planned [23][24][25].

bear.story: The AI-CPU shortage eases or 18A/14A yields or customer wins slip while capex rises sharply in 2027. Intel may also issue more equity off the open S-3ASR shelf after the lock-up ends at the Q3 print [22]. The multiple compresses toward 25x on about $2.40 EPS, a July-2026-style 40%+ drawdown that does not recover. My base-rate sample shows about a 20% chance of a 30%+ loss after a +150% year, and the 2000 analog is far worse [17][19]. I no longer lean on the thin 2027 recession market (~$10k volume) [11], which the supervisor rightly discounted.

base.story: EPS keeps rising toward $2.70 FY28E, but the multiple de-rates from about 58x to 35-40x as growth normalizes. Dilution is limited to RSUs and escrow releases. The stock chops in the $85-140 range it has held since April and ends a little below today.

bull.story: Momentum continues, as it has for the median large-cap semi after a +150% year [17]. Intel lands external 14A foundry customers on top of the Google/Tesla deals [8], FY28 EPS heads past $3.50, and the market holds about 50x.

thesis_break_reason: $72 is below the July-2026 low of $81.79 and about 24% under the $95 price of the August 2026 offering ($23B gross, 242.1M shares including the greenshoe) [19][6][22]. At $72 the stock would trade at about 35x FY27 consensus EPS. Getting there would most likely take falling estimates (AI-CPU demand normalizing, 18A/14A yield or customer setbacks, margins stalling near 40%), not just multiple compression. July 2026 showed that ordinary de-rating on valuation worries stops in the low $80s, so a break below that, with $23B of fresh equity already on the balance sheet, would signal a fundamental problem.

reasoning: Round-2 revision. I verified the supervisor's main correction in the primary filings. There is no planned ~$15B follow-on: $15B was the proposed size of the August deal [23], which was upsized to $20B [24], and the 31.6M-share greenshoe was exercised on Aug 11 [6]. That leaves 5,285M basic shares and $22.62B net proceeds [22], and EDGAR shows no later offering filing [25]. The 424B5 also lists $15.6B of NCI and 143M escrow shares [22], which I had left out. Net effect on fair value: removing the phantom dilution helps, while the NCI, the higher H2 net debt and the escrow shares hurt, so fair value goes from $99 to $96. Starting point is unchanged: INTC is $120 after +258% in a year and +34% in September, at about 58x FY27 consensus EPS of $2.06 and about 11x sales, near the top of its decade P/S range [1][2][4][5]. Base rates (own computation, 28 large semis/tech names [17]): after a +150% trailing year the median next-12-month return was +48% (n=243), or +25% for the post-2002 ex-mega-winner subset (n=72), with a log SD of 0.63-0.82 and about 19% of cases losing more than 30%. Survivorship bias is heavy, so I cut the momentum drift to about 0-10%. Valuation pulls the other way: fair value of about $96 is 20% below spot, and Intel's 2000 peak at about 50x was followed by -82% [19]. Sell-side consensus of about $116, with 32 of 48 at Hold [1][10], agrees with a flat-to-down center. Manifold's 41% on touching $150 by end-2026 [15] is a bit below a driftless touch model (~55%). Per the source review, I now give no weight to the thin 2027 Polymarket markets (~$10k volume) [11][13]. That removes a little of the bear tail I had attributed to macro. Removing the supply overhang of a phantom follow-on is a small positive for the 12-month path. Together these move my median from $112 to $113. I keep sigma at 0.65 (between the base-rate sample's 0.63-0.82 and slightly below the 76% realized vol, since vol mean-reverts after spikes). Result: P(>=120) is 46%, P(>=60) is 84%, and P(>=300) is 7%. The scenario mean (0.25x$60 + 0.5x$110 + 0.25x$185 = $116) is consistent. I agree with the supervisor's factual corrections. I keep my own ladder rather than the forecaster mean because my base-rate evidence still argues for fatter tails on both sides. Research limits: round-1 data constraints (Twelve Data paywall, Alpha Vantage rate limit) still apply, and round 2 used 7 targeted fetches (EDGAR, 424B5, 8-K, Intel IR).
